**What changed:** Angular 20.2 deprecates the entire `@angular/animations` package, with intent to remove it in v22.2 (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/9766116cea69607d80144251a599f1cc1b12e02c, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62795 — "DEPRECATED: @angular/animations"). The replacement is a compiler-level feature (not directives): `animate.enter` and `animate.leave`, which add enter/leave CSS classes at the right time or invoke functions for third-party libraries; they work on elements and as host bindings, accept a space-separated class string or a string array, and support event binding syntax whose `$event` is an `AnimationCallbackEvent` exposing the target element and an `animationComplete()` function (mandatory to call for `animate.leave`; otherwise Angular auto-completes after a 4-second delay, configurable via the `MAX_ANIMATION_TIMEOUT` token in ms) (https://angular.dev/guide/animations). Legacy `@angular/animations` and the new features cannot be mixed **within the same component** (nor across content projection between such components); mixing at application scope is fine (https://angular.dev/guide/animations). **Affects:** Applications that depend on `@angular/animations` / `@angular/platform-browser/animations` (e.g. `provideAnimations()`, `provideAnimationsAsync()`) or that use `trigger`, `transition`, `state`, `:enter`, `:leave` in component metadata. **Action:** required: no change is needed to keep building on 20.2 — the package still ships. Plan the migration away from `@angular/animations` before v22.2: re-implement animations as CSS classes/transitions/keyframes driven by `animate.enter="..."` / `animate.leave="..."` (or `[animate.enter]` / `(animate.leave)` bindings), call `animationComplete()` on the `AnimationCallbackEvent` for JS-driven leave animations, and do not combine legacy animations with `animate.enter`/`animate.leave` in one component or across projected content. **Before/after:** ```html @if (display()) {
Content
}
Content
```

**What changed:** The Angular HTML lexer (`packages/compiler/src/ml_parser/lexer.ts`) previously stopped reading an attribute name as soon as it hit a name-ending character such as `/` or `>` (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62742). In 20.2.0, when an attribute name starts with `[` (`chars.$LBRACKET`), the tokenizer uses a new permissive `nameEndPredicate` that tracks bracket depth and only applies `isNameEnd` when brackets are balanced/mismatched, interrupting on new lines (`chars.isNewLine`), so previously-invalid bound attribute names now parse — e.g. `[class.text-primary/80]`, `[class.data-active:text-green-300/80]`, `[class.data-[size='large']:p-8]`, which compile to `$r3$.ɵɵclassProp("text-primary/80", ctx.expr)(...)` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/7767aa640c542f5058df9322f2bbe974fa8d3c81). This fixes #61671 (Tailwind-style class names in `[class.*]` bindings and in `host: {'[class.…]': …}`) (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/61671). Note the caveat visible in the golden output: in a `host` binding, `[class.data-[size='large']:p-8]` is truncated to the property `"class.data-[size='large'"` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/7767aa640c542f5058df9322f2bbe974fa8d3c81). Listed under `compiler` fixes in the 20.2.0 changelog (2025-08-20) (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.2.0/CHANGELOG.md). **Affects:** Templates and `host` bindings using square-bracketed (bound) attribute names containing characters that used to end the name (`/`, `:`, `[`, `]`, `'`, spaces, etc.), e.g. Tailwind classes in `[class.*]` bindings; also any template that previously relied on the parser stopping at such a character inside a `[`-prefixed attribute name (permissive parsing now ends only at a balanced `]`-then-name-end, or at a newline). **Action:** none — no code, config or dependency change is required; behavior only becomes more permissive. Applications that intentionally worked around the old parse error (e.g. `ngClass` instead of `[class.*]`) may re-verify those bindings. Re-verify templates with malformed/unclosed `[`-prefixed attributes, since names with mismatched brackets are now consumed more greedily (e.g. `[class.a]b]c]`). **Before/after:** ```html
``` ```js // $r3$.ɵɵclassProp("text-primary/80", ctx.expr)("data-active:text-green-300/80", ctx.expr)("data-[size='large']:p-8", ctx.expr); ```

**What changed:** Angular 20.2 adds a new extended diagnostic — error code `8117` (`UNINVOKED_FUNCTION_IN_TEXT_INTERPOLATION` in `packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/diagnostics/src/error_code.ts`) — that reports when a function referenced in a text interpolation is not called, e.g. `

{{ firstName }}

` instead of `

{{ firstName() }}

` (commit 5abfe4a899, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/5abfe4a8999e42ad44e6f1d4414f241094bb8fdb; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.2.0/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/diagnostics/src/error_code.ts). The PR body says a warning is triggered and the change is explicitly non-breaking (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59191). The check's configuration name is `uninvokedFunctionInTextInterpolation`, documented as "NG8117: Functions should be invoked in text interpolation."; `strictTemplates` must be enabled for any extended diagnostic to emit, and this check has no additional requirements beyond `strictTemplates`; it can be disabled by editing the project's `tsconfig.json` extended-diagnostic configuration (https://angular.dev/extended-diagnostics/NG8117). Note: the PR text mentions "NG8114", but in the shipped 20.2 code `8114` is `UNPARENTHESIZED_NULLISH_COALESCING`; the new diagnostic actually ships as NG8117. **Affects:** Applications with `strictTemplates` enabled (extended diagnostics on) whose templates interpolate a function without invoking it, e.g. `{{ firstName }}`. Builds/language service will surface new warnings; the diagnostic is a warning, not a compile error. **Action:** required: re-verify builds for new NG8117 warnings; fix affected templates by invoking the interpolated function (e.g. `{{ firstName() }}`), or disable `uninvokedFunctionInTextInterpolation` via the extended-diagnostic settings in `tsconfig.json` if it cannot be avoided. **Before/after:** ```angular-html

{{ firstName }}

{{ firstName() }}

```

**What changed:** `@angular/compiler-cli` now ignores diagnostics on `ngTemplateContextGuard` lines in the Type Check Block (TCB). Previously, if a directive was deprecated (using `@deprecated` JSDoc) and used in a template with a structural directive (e.g., `*my-directive`), TypeScript would report a deprecation diagnostic on the entire element, from start to end tag, because the deprecation was applied to the directive class and the TCB guard line `if (i1.NgForOf.ngTemplateContextGuard(_t8, _t9) /*331,378*/) {...}` spans the element. The fix calls `markIgnoreDiagnostics(guardInvoke)` on the guard invocation in `packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/src/type_check_block.ts`, preventing the deprecation from leaking onto the whole element in editor suggestion diagnostics (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/63054, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/812463c5636effe5bd5ba5c7c7fc65c3cc08d047, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/63054.diff) **Affects:** Applications using directives with `ngTemplateContextGuard` that are marked as deprecated. Previously, the deprecation warning would incorrectly highlight the entire element in templates; this fix suppresses those false-positive or overly-broad warnings in the Angular Language Service (https://github.com/angular/vscode-ng-language-service/issues/2203) **Action:** none **Before/after:** ```typescript // Before: Deprecation diagnostic reported on the entire element due to the guard line in TCB
Test
// After: No diagnostic reported on the element for the directive's deprecation in the context guard
Test
```

**What changed:** Angular 20.2.0 added support for binding ARIA attributes using standard property binding syntax `[name]="expr"` without the `attr.` prefix. Syntaxes like `[aria-label]="expr"` or `[ariaLabel]="expr"` now bind to the HTML attribute (e.g., `aria-label`) instead of the DOM property (e.g., `ariaLabel`), unless a matching `@Input` or directive input exists (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62630). This mapping uses the DOM schema registry from the compiler (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62630). The change explicitly improves Server-Side Rendering (SSR) where emulated DOM may not reflect ARIA properties as attributes (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62630). The `attr.` syntax remains valid and behaves identically for ARIA attributes.

**Affects:** Applications binding to ARIA attributes (e.g., `aria-label`, `aria-expanded`) using property binding syntax `[aria-label]="..."` or `[ariaLabel]="..."` instead of `[attr.aria-label]="..."`, or applications relying on `[attr.aria-...]` bindings on directives/components that define matching `@Input` properties (e.g. a component with `@Input() ariaLabel`).

**Action:**
*   **If you previously used `[attr.aria-*]` to bypass property binding warnings on elements/components that actually define matching `@Input`s:** The behaviour changes such that the property binding will now target the `@Input` instead of the attribute in some edge cases, though generally `attr.` takes precedence or is equivalent. If you relied on `[attr.aria-label]` specifically to ignore an input and write to the attribute, verify this still works as intended, as the binding logic for ARIA properties is now normalized to prefer attributes unless an input matches (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62630).
*   **If you used `[aria-label]` (without `attr.`):** This now works and is recommended. No code change required, but you can optionally remove `attr.` from existing bindings.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- Before: Required attr. prefix for ARIA attributes to avoid binding to non-existent properties or for SSR correctness -->
<button [attr.aria-label]="myLabel">Button</button>

<!-- After: ARIA attributes can be bound directly; binds to the HTML attribute -->
<button [aria-label]="myLabel">Button</button>

<!-- Both are valid. If a component has @Input() ariaLabel, [aria-label] binds to the Input. -->
```

**What changed:** A bug fix in `@angular/core` for the new `animate.enter` / `animate.leave` API when used with **event binding syntax** (e.g. `(animate.leave)="rotate($event)"`, `(animate.enter)="..."`). Previously, when an `@if`-controlled element with an event-bound `animate.leave` was toggled off and back on faster than the leave animation completed (especially when the exit animation is longer than the enter animation), an extra copy of the element was inserted into the DOM while the original was still running its leave animation, leaving duplicate elements on screen (issue #63127). The fix "applies the same fix that fixed the class version to the event binding version", preventing duplicate elements when animations are toggled too fast (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/63216, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/bdc31675b7e5f37d2b312c766fe4963305620bdf, https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/63127). The event bindings receive an `$event` of type `AnimationCallbackEvent`, whose `animationComplete()` must be called for Angular to remove the element, otherwise removal happens after a 4-second `MAX_ANIMATION_TIMEOUT` delay (https://angular.dev/guide/animations). **Affects:** Applications on 20.2 using `(animate.enter)` / `(animate.leave)` event bindings (JS/third-party library animations, e.g. GSAP) on elements removed via `@if`, particularly where exit animations are slower or toggling is rapid. **Action:** none — this is an internal bug fix, not a breaking change (PR checklist: "No"). Applications using event-bound enter/leave animations should simply re-verify that rapid toggling no longer leaves duplicate elements in the DOM. **Before/after:** ```html @if (isOpen()) {
Content
} ```

**What changed:** In Angular 20.2.0, the compiler feature `animate.leave` was fixed so that space-separated class strings, e.g. `class-1 class-2`, are applied as multiple classes when an element leaves the DOM. Previously `animate.leave` lost that functionality in a refactor; it treated the whole string as a single token, causing `InvalidCharacterError: Failed to execute 'add' on 'DOMTokenList': The token provided ... contains HTML space characters` in `NoneEncapsulationDomRenderer.addClass` (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/62964, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62979). This restores parity with `animate.enter`, which already accepted a single class string with multiple classes separated by spaces or an array of class strings (https://angular.dev/guide/animations). **Affects:** Applications using the 20.2 `animate.leave` attribute on an element with a multi-class value, either a space-separated string like `animate.leave="class-1 class-2"` or a binding that evaluates to such a string. Single-class values are unaffected. **Action:** none **Before/after:** ```html
...
...
``` (Copied structure from https://angular.dev/guide/animations)

**What changed:** The new `animate.enter` / `animate.leave` instructions (added in 20.1 by commit `6b1f4b9e8b`) previously waited indefinitely for an `animationstart`/`transitionstart` event before removing the element (leave) or the animation classes (enter). If the classes referenced by `animate.enter`/`animate.leave` produce no CSS animation or transition — e.g. animations are intentionally suppressed via selector specificity such as an `.animate-disabled` class on a parent node — the node was never removed / classes never cleaned up. `f9d73cc687` in 20.2.0 makes `ɵɵanimateEnter` and `animateLeaveClassRunner` (in `packages/core/src/render3/instructions/animation.ts`) call `determineLongestAnimation` inside a `requestAnimationFrame` after adding the classes; when the element has no entry in the `longestAnimations` map, the enter classes are removed via `renderer.removeClass` + `cleanupEnterClassData`, and for leave the leaving nodes are cleared (`clearLeavingNodes`) and `finalRemoveFn()` runs immediately (`https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/f9d73cc6877d516da4ab4704c21bb19164123fa1.diff`, `https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/63242`). `determineLongestAnimation` in `packages/core/src/animation/longest_animation.ts` no longer takes the `AnimationEvent | TransitionEvent` argument and the `animationstart`/`transitionstart` listeners were dropped (`same diff`). Fixes `#63161`, a request for an alternative to `[@.disabled]` for the new syntax; `@angular/animations` is deprecated in 20.2.0 (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.2.0/CHANGELOG.md`). **Affects:** Only applications that already use the 20.1 `animate.enter` / `animate.leave` attributes, and specifically ones whose animation classes can resolve to no CSS animation/transition at runtime (disabled via CSS specificity, typos/nonexistent class names, or `animationsEnabled: false`-style suppression). The PR is marked as not a breaking change. Tests that manually dispatch `animationstart`/`transitionstart` to drive these animations are affected: the internal tests were rewritten to use `fakeAsync` and tick animation frames instead of dispatching `AnimationEvent('animationstart')` (diff, `packages/core/test/acceptance/animation_spec.ts`). **Action:** none — no code, template or dependency change is required. Re-verify any `animate.enter`/`animate.leave` usages that relied on Angular holding a node/class indefinitely when no matching CSS animation exists, and re-verify unit tests that fake animation progress by dispatching `animationstart`/`transitionstart` (these events are no longer listened for; use `fakeAsync` and tick `requestAnimationFrame`s, which tests treat as 16.6 ms). **Before/after:** ```html
@if (show()) {

I should fade

}
- paragragh.nativeElement.dispatchEvent(new AnimationEvent('animationstart')); expect(fixture.nativeElement.outerHTML).toContain('class="fade"'); ```

**What changed:** When a CSS leave animation is running and an `@if` block is toggled true again (or an `@for` list adds and removes items), Angular previously inserted a fresh enter node while the old leaving node was still animating out, so both nodes were briefly visible in the DOM at once. The fix makes the enter instruction retain a reference to the leaving element(s) per `TNode` and, on enter, dispatch a `CustomEvent` of type `animationend` with `detail: {cancel: true}` on the former node (ending its animation and removing it immediately) before the new node is inserted. This applies to the CSS class-based animation instructions `animate.enter` and `animate.leave` (the `ɵɵanimateEnter` / `ɵɵanimateLeave` functions). Previously this duplication was considered expected native CSS behaviour; the issue was reported as "Two elements appear when leave animation is running and `@if` is toggled true" (#63020) (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/63048, https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/63020, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/6a1184600ce0fc7a3f338d6766612e9510ef5518/packages/animations/browser/src/render/animation_engine_next.ts and the PR diff at https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/angular/angular/pull/63048.diff). **Affects:** Applications using CSS class-based animations via the `animate.enter` / `animate.leave` attributes on elements inside `@if` or `@for` templates, where the leave animation duration is long enough that the block can be re-toggled (or the `@for` list re-added) before the leave animation finishes. **Action:** none (behavioural bug fix; re-verify that toggling `@if` / `@for` with leave animations no longer shows two simultaneous nodes). **Before/after:** ```html
@if (show()) {

I should slide in

}
```

I have the key facts from the commit patch and PR. Writing up now.

**What changed:** An internal feature-detection check in `@angular/core`'s animation instructions was made more robust. Previously, the module-level constant `areAnimationSupported` in `packages/core/src/render3/instructions/animation.ts` tested `typeof document.body !== 'undefined' && typeof document.body.getAnimations === 'function'`. The commit `063b5e166f` ("fix(core): switch check to documentElement with chaining", PR #62773) replaced those two lines with a single optional-chained check: `typeof document?.documentElement?.getAnimations === 'function'`. The PR description states: "This fixes a situation where DOM checks may report null." (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/063b5e166f66bce1abd06c258242212009e76cca, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62773) The check remains guarded by `(typeof ngServerMode === 'undefined' || !ngServerMode) && typeof document !== 'undefined'`.

**Affects:** No application code. This is a purely internal fix in `@angular/core` animation support detection; it only changes behaviour in environments where `document`/`document.body` could be null at module load (e.g. certain non-browser or early-DOM contexts), where animation support detection could previously throw or report `null` instead of falling back to the no-op path.

**Action:** none — upgrading applications need no code, configuration, or dependency changes beyond the version bump itself.

**Before/after:**
```diff
--- a/packages/core/src/render3/instructions/animation.ts
+++ b/packages/core/src/render3/instructions/animation.ts
   typeof document !== 'undefined' &&
-  typeof document.body !== 'undefined' &&
-  typeof document.body.getAnimations === 'function';
+  typeof document?.documentElement?.getAnimations === 'function';
```

**What changed:** `HttpResponse`, `HttpErrorResponse` and their shared `HttpResponseBase` gained a new optional readonly property `redirected?: boolean` (also accepted in their constructor/`clone()` init hashes), mirroring the Fetch API's `Response.redirected` flag. Per the source: "Indicates whether the HTTP response was redirected during the request. This property is only available when using the Fetch API using `withFetch()`. When using the default XHR Request this property will be `undefined`" (). `FetchBackend` was updated to capture and forward the `redirected` flag from the native fetch response; this builds on PR #62315, which added the `redirect` request option (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62675). Community write-ups describe uses like detecting redirects for security checks, analytics logging, and conditional handling (https://angular.love/angular-20-2-the-recent-changes).

**Affects:** Applications using `HttpClient` with the `withFetch` provider that want to read redirect information; purely additive — existing code compiles and behaves identically. Note `redirected` is `undefined` with the default XHR backend.

**Action:** none (optional: read `response.redirected` when using `withFetch()`, which requires `observe: 'response'` to access the full `HttpResponse`).

**Before/after:**
```typescript
// packages/common/http/src/response.ts (v20.2.0)
/**
 * Indicates whether the HTTP response was redirected during the request.
 * This property is only available when using the Fetch API using `withFetch()`
 * When using the default XHR Request this property will be `undefined`
 */
readonly redirected?: boolean;
```

**What changed:** In 20.1.0, `feat(http): Add timeout option to HTTP requests` (#57194) added a `timeout?: number` request option implemented in the XHR and fetch backends, but `HttpClient`'s method overloads (`request`, `get`, `delete`, `head`, `options`, `patch`, and the `addBody` helper) did not declare or forward it, so `http.get('/api/config', {timeout: 3000})` failed to compile with `TS2769: No overload matches this call ... 'timeout' does not exist in type ...` (#62581). In 20.2.0, commit 1408baff / PR #62586 adds `timeout?: number;` to every `HttpClient` overload options object in `packages/common/http/src/client.ts` (and the public API goldens `goldens/public-api/common/http/index.api.md`), adds `transferCache?: {includeHeaders?: string[]} | boolean;` to the `delete` signatures where it was missing, and `addBody` now forwards both `transferCache: options.transferCache` and `timeout: options.timeout` to the backends, so the option actually takes effect (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/1408baff453e636da05838fa17c6e4abd86c4b72, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/62586, https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/62581).

**Affects:** Applications on 20.1.x that pass `timeout` (or `transferCache` on `delete`) in `HttpClient` options objects — e.g. `timeout` caused a TS2769 compile error and was silently dropped by `addBody` where it did compile (also for `keepalive`, `priority`, `cache`, `mode`, `redirect` forwarding via `addBody` for methods with bodies).

**Action:** required: re-verify that requests using the `timeout` option (per ) now compile without TS2769 and that timeouts actually abort requests in both the XHR and fetch backends; re-verify `transferCache` behaviour on `HttpClient#delete`. No code, dependency or configuration edits are needed — the option syntax is unchanged.

**Before/after:**
```ts
// 20.1: compiles with TS2769 ('timeout' not in overload options) and is not passed to backends
// 20.2: valid; HttpClient addBody forwards the values:
return {
  body,
  headers: options.headers,
  context: options.context,
  observe: options.observe,
  params: options.params,
  reportProgress: options.reportProgress,
  responseType: options.responseType,
  withCredentials: options.withCredentials,
  transferCache: options.transferCache,
  timeout: options.timeout,
  keepalive: options.keepalive,
  priority: options.priority,
  cache: options.cache,
  mode: options.mode,
  redirect: options.redirect,
};
```

**What changed:** Angular 20.2 adds template "suggestion diagnostics" to the Angular Language Service, so usages of deprecated APIs inside templates are now surfaced in the IDE (strikethrough/deprecated styling) the same way TypeScript reports deprecated symbols in `.ts` files. The `TemplateTypeChecker` interface gains `getSuggestionDiagnosticsForFile(sf: ts.SourceFile, tsLs: ts.LanguageService, optimizeFor: OptimizeFor): ts.DiagnosticWithLocation[]` and `getSuggestionDiagnosticsForComponent(component: ts.ClassDeclaration, tsLs: ts.LanguageService): ts.DiagnosticWithLocation[]`, described as diagnostics that "proactively suggest deprecated, as opposed to diagnostics that indicate potentially incorrect runtime behavior" (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/d64dd27a02630b631bc9890d7292d4683493cb65). Internally it filters TypeScript suggestion diagnostics where `diag.reportsDeprecated !== undefined` and maps them back to template spans; `TemplateDiagnostic` now extends `ts.DiagnosticWithLocation` (previously `ts.Diagnostic`), `makeTemplateDiagnostic` accepts an optional `DeprecatedDiagnosticInfo` argument, and new `PerfPhase` values `TtcSuggestionDiagnostics` and `LsSuggestionDiagnostics` were added. Deprecation is detected from JSDoc `@deprecated` on the class (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/59343). Note from the diff: "For now, we only report deprecations for components" for element tags — non-component directives are skipped because their spans cover the whole element.

**Affects:** IDE/editor experiences using the Angular Language Service (`@angular/language-service`, `vscode-ng-language-service`), and any third-party tool that implements `TemplateTypeChecker` or calls `makeTemplateDiagnostic` (the new interface methods and changed `TemplateDiagnostic` base type are additive/typed changes). Also affects applications that annotate `@Component` classes (or their inputs/methods) with JSDoc `@deprecated` — new squiggles/strikethrough will appear in templates. No change to build, `ng build`, or runtime behaviour; this is not a deprecation *removal*.

**Action:** none — no code, config or dependency change is required. Optionally re-verify that newly reported deprecated-usage warnings in templates are intentional, and that custom Language Service / `TemplateTypeChecker` consumers still compile against the widened `TemplateDiagnostic` type.

**Before/after:**
```ts
// packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/api/api.ts
-export interface TemplateDiagnostic extends ts.Diagnostic {
+export interface TemplateDiagnostic extends ts.DiagnosticWithLocation {

// packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/typecheck/api/checker.ts (new in 20.2)
+  getSuggestionDiagnosticsForFile(
+    sf: ts.SourceFile,
+    tsLs: ts.LanguageService,
+    optimizeFor: OptimizeFor,
+  ): ts.DiagnosticWithLocation[];
+
+  getSuggestionDiagnosticsForComponent(
+    component: ts.ClassDeclaration,
+    tsLs: ts.LanguageService,
+  ): ts.DiagnosticWithLocation[];
```
